title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's second draft of an axiomatic 'analysis situs', a programme toward the 'tame topology' announced in the Esquisse. The basic objects are 'ateliers': posets of 'figures' carrying two relations. The first is ≤ ('subfigure'). The second is << (a coarser 'contained in / dominated by' relation; the crossed-out lines mentioning interiors A° suggest it is defined via interiors or supports). The model example is Fig(L), the atelier of all figures in a set L. A figure Φ is a (finite) family of subsets of L called strata or atoms, with support |Φ|. The point-figure of x ∈ L is Φ_x = {{x}}. The previous page ends by asking which sub-ateliers of Fig(L) arise from 'polyhedral notions'.

This page (Scholie) is a representation statement. Giving a '(quasi-)set-theoretic atelier tending to =' (abstractly) amounts to giving a pair (L, F), where L is a set and F ⊂ Fig(L) is a sub-atelier satisfying:
- Atomes*1: for every x ∈ L, {{x}} ∈ F.

A first, crossed-out version of the axiom was a separation condition: the strata of figures in F separate the points of L, i.e. for x ≠ y there are Φ ∈ F and A ∈ Φ containing exactly one of x, y. This is T0-type separation. It was replaced by the stronger requirement that all point-figures belong to F.

The key verification is that L is recoverable intrinsically from (F, ≤, <<). The map x ↦ Φ_x = {{x}} is a bijection from L onto the set of elements of F∖{∅} that are minimal for <<.
- Φ_x is <<-minimal already in Fig(L)∖{∅}, hence a fortiori in F∖{∅}.
- Conversely, let F be <<-minimal in F∖{∅}. Since F ≠ ∅ we have |F| ≠ ∅. Pick x ∈ |F|; then Φ_x << F (and Φ_x ∈ F by Atomes*1). By minimality, Φ_x = F.

So the 'points' of an abstract atelier are its <<-minimal nonempty figures. This is the reconstruction-of-points step needed to pass between abstract ateliers and concrete (L, F) data.

The next page goes on to axiomatize which F ⊂ Fig(L) are allowed:
- Axiome*2: F is closed under subfigures.
- Axiome*3: F is closed under joins of multistratum-compatible figures.
These are re-expressed through a set M of elementary figures with a reflexive, symmetric 'geometric compatibility' relation.
errors: The minimality argument tacitly uses properties of << not stated on the page. 'Minimal' must mean 'G << F, G ≠ ∅ ⇒ G = F', which requires << to be antisymmetric on point-figures. It also requires (a) Φ_x << F whenever x ∈ |F|, and (b) the only nonempty G with G << Φ_x is Φ_x itself (e.g. no figures with empty strata). These presumably follow from the definition of << given earlier, but are not checked here.
Injectivity of x ↦ Φ_x is trivial; surjectivity onto the minimal elements is what is proved. That argument is fine given the above assumptions.

ideas.what: Abstract 'atelier' (poset of figures with relations ≤ and <<) represented concretely as a sub-atelier F of Fig(L) for a set L, under the axiom that all point-figures {{x}} lie in F
ideas.modern_name: Representation theorem / point reconstruction; analogous to recovering points of a locale or atoms of an atomic lattice (Stone-type duality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936) for Boolean algebras; Ehresmann, Isbell and others for locales and points (pointless topology)
ideas.where_published: The atelier formalism appears only in the unpublished Analysis situs notes (156-x). The Esquisse d'un programme only sketches tame topology programmatically.

ideas.what: Points of the atelier as <<-minimal nonempty figures
ideas.modern_name: Atoms of a poset / minimal elements as points

ideas.what: Discarded alternative axiom: strata of figures separate points (T0-type separation)
ideas.modern_name: T0 separation / point-separating family of sets

missed.claim: The page is one step of an unpublished axiomatics of 'ateliers' of figures intended as a foundation for tame topology. In it, an abstract atelier tending to '=' is shown equivalent to a concrete pair (L, F ⊂ Fig(L)), with points recovered as <<-minimal figures. This combinatorial-axiomatic approach (via figures and stratum compatibility, not definable sets) was not developed in the later literature. That literature (o-minimality, van den Dries 1998; Shiota; stratified spaces) took a model-theoretic route instead. The local step itself is routine.
missed.quote: Se donner un atelier (quasi-)ensembliste, "tendant vers =" que de se donner un couple (L, F), où L est un ens, F un sous-atelier de Fig(L)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing Grothendieck's figure/atelier axioms with o-minimal structures or with pre-o-minimal / tame stratified frameworks could reveal a genuinely different, more combinatorial foundation for tame topology. Its interest lies in the whole manuscript, not this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The result proved on this page is an elementary point-reconstruction lemma. Its only interest is as part of Grothendieck's otherwise unknown 'atelier' axiomatics for tame topology, which is historically notable but not surprising at the level of this page.
transcription_corrections: Crossed-out axiom: '∃ Φ ∈ Φ, A ∈ F' should read '∃ Φ ∈ F, A ∈ Φ, tel qu'on ait x ∈ A, y ∉ A ou y ∈ A, x ∉ A'.
Crossed-out axiom: 'Les [?] atomes des Φ ∈ F séparent les points' — the handwriting suggests 'Les strates des Φ ∈ F séparent les points de L'.
'Le [-...-] est de vérifier' — likely 'Le point est de vérifier' (a word is struck out; uncertain).
'L se reconstitue : partir de' should be 'L se reconstitue à partir de'.
'On soit F ∈ F∖{∅}' should be 'Or soit F ∈ F∖{∅} minimal'.
'minimal2' should be 'minimal (pour <<) dans Fig(L)∖{∅}, a fortiori dans F∖{∅}'.
'comme l'ens des limites de F' — reading uncertain; the intended meaning is the set of <<-minimal elements of F∖{∅}.
